docs.title: Consumer Price Index, Gold Price Index, and US Dollar Price Index in June 2026, Q2 2026, and the first six months of 2026
docs.excerpt:
Consumer Price Index, Gold Price Index, and US Dollar Price Index in June 2026, Q2 2026, and the first six months of 2026
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) in June 2026 recorded a month-on-month decrease of 0.39%, mainly attributable to a decline in gasoline and oil prices in line with global fuel price movements. Compared to December 2025, the CPI in June increased by 3.21% and rose by 4.69% year-on-year.
The CPI in June fell by 0.39% compared to the previous month, with price indices declining in four groups of goods and services, while increasing in seven groups. On average, the CPI in the second quarter of 2026 rose by 5.25% year-on-year. The average CPI for the first six months of 2026 increased by 4.38% compared to the same period last year.
Core inflation in June posted a month-on-month increase of 0.14% and a year-on-year rise of 4.50%. On average, core inflation in the first six months of 2026 went up by 4.12% year-on-year, lower than the 4.38% increase of the overall average CPI.
The gold price index in June declined by 8.46% compared to May; increased by 24.11% year-on-year; and decreased by 2.72% compared to December 2025. On average, the gold price index in the second quarter of 2026 rose by 36.84% year-on-year, while the average index for the first six months of 2026 surged by 58.12% compared to the same period last year.
The US dollar price index in June recorded a month-on-month increase of 0.11%; rose by 0.57% year-on-year; and fell by 0.17% compared to December 2025. On average, the US dollar price index in the second quarter of 2026 increased by 0.93% year-on-year, and the average index for the first six months of 2026 climbed by 1.75%.

docs.title: Report on socio-economic situation in May and five months of 2026
docs.excerpt:
– The disbursed investment from the State budget in May was estimated at nearly 65 trillion VND, a 10.2% growth year-on-year. Generally, in the first five months of 2026, the disbursed State budget investment was estimated at 254.1 trillion VND, equivalent to 24.0% of the annual plan and a year-on-year increase of 11.2% (these figures in 2025 were 22.5% and 21.1%, respectively).
– Total inward foreign investment in Viet Nam as of May 31, 2026, including newly registered capital, adjusting registered capital, and the value of capital contribution and purchasing shares by foreign investors reached 24.81 billion USD, a year-on-year increase of 34.9%.
– Disbursed FDI in Viet Nam during the first five months of 2026 was estimated at 9.75 billion USD, a year-on-year growth of 9.6%.
Total state budget revenue in May 2026 was estimated at nearly 215.0 trillion VND. The accrued revenue in the first 5 months of 2026 reached 1,339.7 trillion VND, reaching 53.0% of the annual estimate (+15.3% YoY).
In May, the total export and import turnover of goods[2] reached 99.07 billion USD, a month-on-month increase of 3.2% and a year-on-year increase of 25.8%. Generally, in the five months of 2026, the total export and import turnover of goods reached 445.12 billion USD, going up 25.0% over that in the same period last year, of which exports increased by 19.5%; and imports increased by 30.8%. The trade balance of goods recorded a trade deficit of 13.80 billion USD.
+ In May 2026, export turnover of goods amounted to 46.93 billion USD, increasing by 2.1% over the previous month and increasing by 18.0% over that in the same period last year. Overall, in the five months of 2026, the export turnover reached 215.66 billion USD, increasing by 19.5% over the same period last year. Of which, the domestic economic sector reached 43.5 billion USD, rose by 2.5%, accounting for 20.2% of total export turnover; the FDI sector (including crude oil) attained 172.16 billion USD, went up by 24.7%, accounting for 79.8%.
+ Import turnover of goods in May 2026 reach 52.14 billion USD, a rise of 4.3% over the previous month and increased by 33.8% year-on-year. Overall, in the five months of 2026, the import turnover of goods reached 229.46 billion USD, a year-on-year surge of 30.8%, of which, the domestic economic sector reached 64.26 billion USD, an upturn of 22.7%; and the FDI sector reached 165.2 billion USD, an expansion of 34.3%.
– Regarding export and import markets of goods in the five months of 2026, the United States was Viet Nam’s largest export market with a turnover of 69.6 billion USD. China remained Viet Nam’s largest import market with a turnover of 92.6 billion USD.
– According to preliminary data, the trade balance of goods in May recorded a deficit of 5.21 billion USD. Overall, in the five months of 2026, the trade balance of goods posted a deficit of 13.80 billion USD (a surplus of 5.1 billion USD in the same period last year). Of which, the domestic economic sector recorded a trade deficit of 20.76 billion USD; while the FDI sector (including crude oil) recorded a trade surplus of 6.96 billion USD.
c) Consumer price index, gold and US dollar price index
[1] The value of export turnover was calculated at F.O.B price and import turnover was calculated at C.I.F price (including transportation and insurance costs of imported goods).
[2] Preliminary data on exports and imports of goods in May 2026 provided by the Viet Nam Customs on 2nd June, 2026.
